text:
mike: Quick heads-up — I ran a weekend batch of the buffer-pool prototype on staging (mixed-seq workloads, KV cache warm). Results are interesting: ~30% fewer OOMs with expandable_segments=1 and max_split_size_mb=128, but P99 token latency increased in some tails. Posting config + short logs below.

mike: config snippet:
```
allocator: pytorch_cuda
expandable_segments: 1
max_split_size_mb: 128
garbage_collection_threshold: 0.15
workspace_initial_mb: 64
reuse_buffer_pool: true
```

sarah: Nice. Can you paste the profiler summary? nvprof/pt-prof? Also which model variants?

mike: nvprof summary (trimmed):
```
GPU memcpy HtoD:  12.3%
GPU memcpy DtoH:  0.5%
Kernel compute:    78.1%
Context switch:     1.2%
```
Alloc/free churn (sampled): 1.2M -> 800k ops per run. Fragmentation metric (free_bytes / total_bytes): 0.18 -> 0.12 after pool.
Model: gpt-medium-rl, seq len burst to 2048 for 5% of requests. KV cache pressure still visible during bursts.

kai: Interesting. So pool reduces alloc churn (good) but P99 regressed — likely due to buffer reuse eviction causing extra memcpy during KV re-materialization on burst. Did you measure memcpy during those tails?

mike: yes — the tails show spikes in HtoD around the burst windows up to 45ms more. Hypothesis: reuse_buffer_pool keeps buffers pinned smaller chunks, forcing extra copies when KV cache needs contiguous workspace for longer seqs.

ben: Two quick experiments to try: lower garbage_collection_threshold to 0.05 to GC faster, and bump workspace_initial_mb to 256 so hot paths avoid reallocation under burst. Also try max_split_size_mb=64 to encourage bigger contiguous allocations rather than lots of small pieces.

mike: ran bench on ruled set:
- run A (base pool cfg above): 30% fewer OOMs, P99 +12ms
- run B (gc=0.05, workspace_initial=256): OOMs same reduction, P99 back to baseline, small increase in avg latency +1.5ms
- run C (max_split_size_mb=64): fragmentation slightly worse, OOM reduction only ~15%

sarah: So best compromise looks like run B. Any secondary effects on memory pressure for other tenants in shared pool?

mike: For dedicated-staging yes fine; in multi-tenant host we saw one case where memory headroom dropped by ~60MB but still within target for Dedicated. For Hosted lanes we probably need stricter caps.

kai: Another angle: make pool eviction LRUness consider KV cache residency tags — if buffer in pool is likely to be used for KV we should avoid reusing it. Might need small tagging on alloc meta.

ben: Agree — tagging would be ideal but invasive. As short term: we can expose workspace_initial_mb and gc threshold via runtime flags per-model. That matches different seq distributions.

infra-bot: deploy-batch: buffer-pool-experiments rollout (staging) succeeded at 2026-03-14T09:12:30Z :thumbsup:

mike: Action items: 1) prototype per-model workspace_initial_mb override (PR draft), 2) try GC threshold 0.05 in prod canary, 3) investigate lightweight tagging for KV residency (tracking ticket). I'll open PR + ticket.

sarah: ack, move to eng-runtime board when ready. Thanks for the writeup! :rocket:
